correspondence.component_scope: Chosen northwestern opening and eastward upper approach
correspondence.finding: The pinned selection opens in the northwestern interior and runs eastward. No permitted original map has established its actual feeder, initial lake or wetland passage, or the entry into the following selected reach.

correspondence.component_scope: Southeastern upper continuation and northern-to-middle transfer
correspondence.finding: The selection bends southeast and continues into the central corridor. Source correspondence for the complete through-link, any intervening lakes or wet ground, and lateral junctions is missing.

correspondence.component_scope: Westward middle bend and return toward the east
correspondence.finding: The selected course bends southwest before returning southeast. No permissible original observation distinguishes a genuine connected river/lake passage from a modeled transfer between neighboring waters.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastward middle passage
correspondence.finding: The selected course follows a comparatively long eastward corridor. Its water-body identities, intervening narrows, lateral joins and connection to the southbound continuation are unestablished.

correspondence.component_scope: Southbound continuation
correspondence.finding: The selection turns south through several short stored parts. Independent cartographic correspondence has not established the continuous channel or any lake/wetland connectors in this portion.

correspondence.component_scope: Southeastern lower approach
correspondence.finding: The selected lower approach runs southeast, turns east, then south. The connected natural watercourse, tributary entries and any distinct named reaches remain unverified.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower southbound reach and actual selected terminal
correspondence.finding: The final selected course turns south and then southeast toward the coastal region. No permitted original map establishes the actual outlet channel, receiving bay, intervening estuarine waters, or the relationship between the last rendered position and the true coastal water passage. The model sea classification is not independent terminal evidence.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual chosen headward opening and small waterbodies
correspondence.finding: The chosen opening is the mapped local drainage near Poço Verde, continuing northeast through the Muriçoca/Aquiraz and Tiraíde road-corridor setting. Small filled waterbodies interrupt the mapped stream. Their connected approach and exit corridors are depicted; no individual reservoir name or present operation is assigned. The separate Ibiapina and Pedra de Fogo waterbodies east of this approach are not inserted into the selection.

correspondence.component_scope: Distinct upper named reach and northern seam
correspondence.finding: The selected upper continuation follows the Jatobá-labelled drainage by Tingui and Pé do Morro toward Água Branca. The municipal footprints and regional sheet establish its northward continuation. Jatobá is retained as a distinct component name; a precise Jatobá-to-Coreaú naming boundary is not asserted.

correspondence.component_scope: Frecheirinha eastern passage
correspondence.finding: The selected route is the eastern river corridor past Caiçara de Cima, the Frecheirinha road-crossing setting and Caiçara de Baixo/Jenipapo. Its joins with local drainage and continuation northeast are visible. The west-side Juazeiro, Lagoa do Barro and other ponds remain separate geographical features.

correspondence.component_scope: Northeastern continuation into Coreaú
correspondence.finding: The state original directly labels and continuously maps the selected river from the Frecheirinha continuation toward Coreaú. Its river bends, town-side passage and northern continuation correspond at regional scale. This interval relies partly on the generalized 1:650,000 sheet; the more detailed Granja sheet overlaps the Coreaú end, rather than supplying nonexistent detailed coverage of the entire southern interval.

correspondence.component_scope: Coreaú, tributary joins and Moraújo
correspondence.finding: The original follows Coreaú past the distinct western Rio Juazeiro approach, through Moraújo and the Enjeitado junction, then past Várzea Redonda and Jordão. Várzea da Volta waterbody to the east and western tributary impoundments are off the selected through-route. No managed transfer is needed to explain the depicted river connection.

correspondence.component_scope: Campanário, Estreito and Palestina
correspondence.finding: The river continues through the Campanário crossing, enlarged channel bends and side-channel reaches toward Estreito and Palestina. Salão/Porcos-side drainage and other local joins are depicted separately. The selected through-course is a continuous mapped river corridor, not an inferred connection between nearby labels; no distinct lake name is assigned to widened reaches.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower bends and Granja passage
correspondence.finding: Adjoining Granja sheets follow the northwestern river bends and the separately mapped Saíri, Campo Grande and Gangorra-side approaches, then the Granja crossing and Cachoeira/Torrão continuation. Sheet overlap and the Camocim original establish the downstream continuation. Adjacent ponds and tributaries are not treated as selected fragments.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower saline and floodplain corridor
correspondence.finding: The named lower river passes the flood-prone/saline mapped landscape near Salina Santo Antônio, Cândido Silva and Morro Vermelho, then the widening channel toward Camocim. Saline areas and side channels are separately visible. The evidence establishes the ordinary through-river geography, not a presently operating saltworks transfer or perennial freshwater continuity.

correspondence.component_scope: True selected coastal terminal
correspondence.finding: The actual final selected part is followed through the Ilha da Trindade estuarine channel setting toward Barra do Camocim and the Atlantic transition northeast of Camocim. The connected estuarine branches are depicted on the original. The endpoint is not relocated to Guriú or another coastal outlet. No exact modern bank, surveyed mouth point or current tidal state is claimed.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual northern selected opening and lake passage
correspondence.finding: The northern blue drainage in Figure 3.3 and the inventory map matches the chosen opening and southeastward approach to the elongated Surasaca lake. The waterbody and its southern continuation are distinguishable in the project maps, including the less symbol-obscured vulnerability map. The initial small channel is not separately named.

correspondence.component_scope: Lake outlet and southward upper valley to Oyón
correspondence.finding: The lake-side southern continuation proceeds through the Fundición/Quichas upper valley toward Oyón. The selected route is distinct from the western Ushpa-side drainage and eastern Pampahuay–Patón branch. Section 3.3.1.5 calls the upper river Quichas until the Oyón/Pampahuay junction setting; it does not supply an exact naming vertex.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper Huaura bend, Churín approach and receiving junctions
correspondence.finding: The selected course turns southwest below Oyón, continues by the Churín setting and joins the eastern Checras drainage before its westward bend near Pampa Libre. The inventory map separates the Pampahuay–Patón, Huaura–Churín and Checras subbasins while showing their actual blue-channel connections. The named tributary branches are not relabeled as the selected trunk.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle southwestern valley and approach to Sayán
correspondence.finding: The continuous receiving channel runs southwest from the western bend past the Pampa Libre/Alco corridor toward Aquia and Sayán. Both the inventory map and the isohyet map expose the intermediate bends and side-drainage joins along the chosen course.

correspondence.component_scope: Sayán junction and westward lower-valley turn
correspondence.finding: The selected northeast approach reaches the Sayán confluence setting and turns west through the Andahuasi valley. The southeastern Río Chico–Auquimarca branch is distinguishable from the selected incoming course and joins the common lower Huaura. The selected westward continuation is visible across the turn and lower tributary junctions.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Huaura and selected Pacific terminal
correspondence.finding: The original maps label the lower westward river Huaura and depict its continuous route through the Humaya/Huaura setting to the Pacific coast. The chosen terminal corresponds to that mouth, rather than to the separate drainage farther south near Huacho. The final westward and southwestward coastal approach is covered.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen western opening and upper Silvies River approach
correspondence.finding: The chosen opening is in the mapped upper Silvies River valley southwest of its Wickiup Creek joining setting. Original cartography labels the river on this northern approach and depicts a connected channel past the Snowshoe Creek, Wickiup Creek and Cold Creek joining settings toward Bear Valley. The simplified initial northeast segment clips local bends and hillsides; this finding establishes the ordinary valley and joining relationships, not an exact all-water straight line or the official ultimate river source.

correspondence.component_scope: Bear Valley eastward bend and southward river
correspondence.finding: The named Silvies River enters the western Bear Valley wetland setting, continues east through a depicted meandering channel, and turns south near Camp Creek and Windy Point. The original shows the Jack Creek, Scotty Creek and Damon Creek joining surroundings and an uninterrupted trunk toward Seneca. Sproul Reservoir is a separate side waterbody in the Hay Creek/Swamp Creek surroundings and is not the selected mainstem passage.

correspondence.component_scope: Seneca, Soda Valley and the upper canyon
correspondence.finding: The river receives the Bear Creek channel north of Seneca and continues through Seneca into Soda Valley. Mapped river water and successive canyon bends establish the selected southward route past Soda Spring and Fisk Gulch to the Silvies valley. Southworth Ditch is distinguished from Bear Creek. Pronghorn Reservoir lies east of the selected trunk and is not a through-reservoir component.

correspondence.component_scope: Silvies valley and the westward canyon turn
correspondence.finding: The mapped Silvies River continues south past Silvies and its airport, the Jump Creek and Bridge Creek surroundings, then through the broad wetland valley across the Grant–Harney county boundary. Buffalo Lake lies west of the river and is not a selected lake crossing. Near the Trout Creek joining setting, the selected river turns west into the canyon; the original depicts the river connection itself rather than merely a valley label.

correspondence.component_scope: Canyon through the western bend and lower north–south reach
correspondence.finding: The original river continues west and southwest past the Boulder Creek, Bellows Creek, Sage Hen Creek and Starrcliff Creek joining settings, then through the major western bend below the Myrtle Creek surroundings. It subsequently turns south along a confined valley and receives the Emigrant Creek and Landing Creek approaches. The selected geometry clips individual canyon meanders, while the continuous mapped channel establishes the same ordinary through-corridor. These tributaries retain separate identities.

correspondence.component_scope: Silvies Canyon and the approach to Burns
correspondence.finding: The selected main corridor continues through Silvies Canyon, the Charlie Creek joining setting and the Thousand Spring Creek surroundings into the broad valley north of Burns. The original distinguishes the Silvies River trunk, Foley Slough and other floodplain channels. Arntz Reservoir and Paiute Reservoir are separately mapped side waterbodies, not selected through-reservoir passages. The main trunk is established to the Burns-area wetland setting; the subsequent modeled eastern route is considered separately below.

correspondence.component_scope: Burns wetland passage toward the eastern branch network
correspondence.finding: The source distinguishes the Silvies River through Burns, the named East Fork farther south, Foley Slough east of the trunk and Embree Slough farther east. The selected route leaves the established trunk corridor, crosses the Burns-area marsh between the separately depicted channels and heads toward the Embree Slough surroundings. The inspected originals show wetlands, drainage lines and canals but do not establish all of this selected through-transfer. Marsh symbols, common basin context and the nearby East Fork name are not treated as a substitute for the missing connection.

correspondence.component_scope: Embree Slough, East Fork and the lower southeast corridor
correspondence.finding: Embree Slough is separately labelled and its lower channel joins the East Fork Silvies River near the Embree Bridge Road setting. The original shows the East Fork continuing southeast through the broad wetland corridor toward Lawen and South Harney Road. These local channels and their joining relationship are supported, while the preceding selected Burns-to-Embree passage remains unresolved. West Fork Silvies River is a distinct western channel, not an alternate label applied indiscriminately to the East Fork.

correspondence.component_scope: East Fork, Square Well Slough and Black Slough surroundings
correspondence.finding: The detailed original distinguishes the East Fork continuing east and southeast, Square Well Slough in its looped western setting and Black Slough in the intervening wetland network. A mapped side-channel relationship and the named slough surroundings can be read, but they do not establish the selected southward through-passage from this network toward the West Fork. The selected extension crosses intervening patchy wetland, channel and non-wetland terrain; no continuous corresponding transfer is established by the regional or final detailed original.

correspondence.component_scope: West Fork approach, lake-margin wetland and actual terminal
correspondence.finding: The source clearly labels West Fork Silvies River near Lawen Lane and in the northern Malheur Lake wetland fringe. The actual selected endpoint is inside the cartographically depicted Malheur Lake waterbody. This terminal identification comes from the inspected original and the supplied endpoint location, rather than substituting a familiar closed-basin lake. However, the unresolved incoming transfer from the East Fork/Black Slough surroundings and the full selected continuation across the lake-margin wetland are not established as a continuous source-depicted route. The mapped lake extent is cartographic evidence, not a statement of current water level or contemporary shoreline.
